items.readable_text:
Content:
In a relationship between two variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] a line of best fit (or trend line) captures the general direction of the data, even if no single data point lies exactly on it.

Content:
But how should we interpret the line in relation to the actual data points?

Content:
We do so using the line's predictions.
A data point's predicted [MATH: y]-value is the [MATH: y]-value of the point on the line of best fit at the same [MATH: x]-coordinate as the point.

Content:
Consider the scatter plot below, which shows [MATH: 10] data points in the relationship between two variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] along with a line of best fit.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/645c0c593d1c805e8f847241ae4bc92d]

Content:
The line of best fit provides an overall model of the data, but it is not exact for every individual point:

Content:
- A data point's actual [MATH: y]-value [MATH: (y_\text{true})] is less than the [MATH: y]-value predicted by the line of best fit [MATH: (y_\text{pred})] if it lies below this line.

[IMG: /graphics/57da96c180109dfbd37a9365b38a9f80]

Since the predicted [MATH: y]-value is greater than the actual [MATH: y]-value ([MATH: y_\text{pred} > y_\text{true}]), the line of best fit overestimates these data points. In this case, there is a total of [MATH: 6] data points below the line.

Content:
- On the other hand, a data point's actual [MATH: y]-value [MATH: (y_\text{true})] is greater than the [MATH: y]-value predicted by the line of best fit [MATH: (y_\text{pred})] if it lies above this line.

[IMG: /graphics/0168990cc92beeb7762c750d70db22a1]

Since the predicted [MATH: y]-value is less than the actual [MATH: y]-value ([MATH: y_\text{pred} < y_\text{true}]), the line of best fit underestimates these data points. In this case, there is a total of [MATH: 4] data points above the line.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In a relationship between two variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] a line of best fit (or trend line) captures the general direction of the data, even if no single data point lies exactly on it.

Content:
But how should we interpret the line in relation to the actual data points?

Content:
We do so using the line's predictions.
A data point's predicted [MATH: y]-value is the [MATH: y]-value of the point on the line of best fit at the same [MATH: x]-coordinate as the point.

Content:
Consider the scatter plot below, which shows [MATH: 10] data points in the relationship between two variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] along with a line of best fit.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/645c0c593d1c805e8f847241ae4bc92d]

Content:
The line of best fit provides an overall model of the data, but it is not exact for every individual point:

Content:
- A data point's actual [MATH: y]-value [MATH: (y_\text{true})] is less than the [MATH: y]-value predicted by the line of best fit [MATH: (y_\text{pred})] if it lies below this line.

[IMG: /graphics/57da96c180109dfbd37a9365b38a9f80]

Since the predicted [MATH: y]-value is greater than the actual [MATH: y]-value ([MATH: y_\text{pred} > y_\text{true}]), the line of best fit overestimates these data points. In this case, there is a total of [MATH: 6] data points below the line.

Content:
- On the other hand, a data point's actual [MATH: y]-value [MATH: (y_\text{true})] is greater than the [MATH: y]-value predicted by the line of best fit [MATH: (y_\text{pred})] if it lies above this line.

[IMG: /graphics/0168990cc92beeb7762c750d70db22a1]

Since the predicted [MATH: y]-value is less than the actual [MATH: y]-value ([MATH: y_\text{pred} < y_\text{true}]), the line of best fit underestimates these data points. In this case, there is a total of [MATH: 4] data points above the line.

---

Item 2 — Example: Counting the Number of Points Underestimated or Overestimated by a Line of Best Fit

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/aec21fba05996faf931d90dc5bd02758]

The scatter plot above shows [MATH: 9] data points in the relationship between two variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] along with a line of best fit. For how many of the [MATH: 9] data points is the actual [MATH: y]-value less than the [MATH: y]-value predicted by the line of best fit?

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
A data point's predicted [MATH: y]-value is the [MATH: y]-value of the point on the line of best fit at the same [MATH: x]-coordinate as the point.

A data point's actual [MATH: y]-value is less than the [MATH: y]-value predicted by the line of best fit if it lies below this line.

[IMG: /graphics/f711e62fe79200b91defe1e60caa3424]

Counting all such cases gives a total of [MATH: 3] data points below the line.

Therefore, the number of data points with an actual [MATH: y]-value less than the [MATH: y]-value predicted by the line of best fit is [MATH: 3.]

Item 8 — Tutorial: Identifying Differences

Content:
The scatter plot below shows several data points in the relationship between two variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] along with a line of best fit.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/e21dd4937d6d518ce4eaaecb4081e2f1]

Content:
Let's determine whether any of the labeled data points [MATH: A,] [MATH: B,] or [MATH: C] has an actual [MATH: y]-value that is at least [MATH: 10] more than the value predicted by the line of best fit.

Content:
First, recall the following:

Content:
- A data point's predicted [MATH: y]-value is the [MATH: y]-value of the point on the line of best fit at the same [MATH: x]-coordinate as the point.
- A data point's actual [MATH: y]-value is greater than the [MATH: y]-value predicted by the line of best fit if it lies above this line.

Content:
With that in mind, let's consider each of the given points in turn.

Content:
- First, consider data point [MATH: A] with coordinates [MATH: (15,60).] At [MATH: x=15,] the line of best fit predicts a corresponding [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: y\approx 49.]

[IMG: /graphics/8facaf788e316d400e7e8cee173bfe39]

On the other hand, the actual [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: A] is [MATH: y=60.] So, the difference between the actual and predicted [MATH: y]-values is
[MATH: 60 - 49 = 11 \geq 10.]
Hence, the actual [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: A] is at least [MATH: 10] more than the predicted [MATH: y]-value.
- Next, consider data point [MATH: B] with coordinates [MATH: (20,50).] Since [MATH: B] lies below the line, its [MATH: y]-value is less than the value predicted by the line of best fit, not greater than.

[IMG: /graphics/f4dff38d1b9e2e5985634dcf4ed193d9]

Hence, the actual [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: B] is not at least [MATH: 10] more than the predicted [MATH: y]-value.
- Finally, consider data point [MATH: C] with coordinates [MATH: (21,70).] At [MATH: x=21,] the line of best fit predicts a corresponding [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: y \approx 62.]

[IMG: /graphics/0a5910135b07bf8e4b1867c50a758aec]

On the other hand, the actual [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: C] is [MATH: y=70.] So, the difference between the actual and predicted [MATH: y]-values is
[MATH: 70 - 62 = 8 \not\geq 10.]
Hence, the actual [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: C] is not at least [MATH: 10] more than the predicted [MATH: y]-value.

Content:
Therefore, only the [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: A] is at least [MATH: 10] more than the value predicted by the line of best fit.

Item 9 — Example: Identifying Data Points Corresponding to a Minimum Underestimate or Overestimate

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/48e37d715519c5aebc3828a647e4ddfe]

The scatter plot above shows several data points in the relationship between two variables [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] along with a line of best fit.
Which of the labeled data points [MATH: A,] [MATH: B,] or [MATH: C] has a [MATH: y]-value that is at least [MATH: 10] less than the value predicted by the line of best fit?

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
A data point's predicted [MATH: y]-value is the [MATH: y]-value of the point on the line of best fit at the same [MATH: x]-coordinate as the point.

A data point's actual [MATH: y]-value is less than the [MATH: y]-value predicted by the line of best fit if it lies below this line.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the given points in turn.

- First, consider data point [MATH: A] with coordinates [MATH: (22,35).] At [MATH: x=22,] the line of best fit predicts a corresponding [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: y \approx 48.]

[IMG: /graphics/a7c8185b2da484f0087dda4b8142d597]

On the other hand, the actual [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: A] is [MATH: y=35.] So, the difference between the actual and predicted [MATH: y]-values is
[MATH: 48 - 35 = 13 \geq 10.]
Hence, the actual [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: A] is at least [MATH: 10] less than the predicted [MATH: y]-value.
- Next, consider data point [MATH: B] with coordinates [MATH: (25,65).] Since [MATH: B] lies above the line, its [MATH: y]-value is greater than the value predicted by the line of best fit, not less than.

[IMG: /graphics/7dcbd9906251d90731f3f8060d1ec499]

Hence, the actual [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: B] is not at least [MATH: 10] less than the predicted [MATH: y]-value.

- Finally, consider data point [MATH: C] with coordinates [MATH: (27,45).] At [MATH: x=27,] the line of best fit predicts a corresponding [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: y \approx 59.]

[IMG: /graphics/72cefb08f90012047a214af30c744ce9]

On the other hand, the actual [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: C] is [MATH: y=45.] So, the difference between the actual and predicted [MATH: y]-values is
[MATH: 59 - 45 = 14 \geq 10.]
Hence, the actual [MATH: y]-value of [MATH: C] is at least [MATH: 10] less than the predicted [MATH: y]-value.

Therefore, the actual [MATH: y]-values of [MATH: A] and [MATH: C] are at least [MATH: 10] less than the predicted [MATH: y]-values.

Item 12 — Example: Identifying the Worst Predicted Data Point

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/043ffcc9b0ef732cd493da34197178b6]

A productivity audit tracked [MATH: 27] workdays. For each workday, the average time in meetings ([MATH: x], in hours) and the average time in focused work ([MATH: y], in hours) were recorded to the nearest half hour. The scatter plot above shows the data with a line of best fit.

The line of best fit overestimates one workday’s reported focused-work time by more than [MATH: 1] hour. How many hours of meetings were recorded this day?

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The line of best fit predicts a day's average time in focused work ([MATH: y]) given its average time in meetings ([MATH: x]).

The line overestimates a day’s reported focused-work time if its corresponding point on the scatter plot lies below the line.

[IMG: /graphics/5bcba8d34741a12a544cfa889c5f47ec]

We are told that, for one of these points, the line of best fit overestimates the day’s reported focused-work time by more than [MATH: 1] hour.

Consider the data point at [MATH: (2,3).] For a day with [MATH: x=2] hours of meetings, the line of best fit predicts approximately [MATH: y \approx 4.2] hours of focused work.

[IMG: /graphics/b7a6fc4bf6189f66a56417d4b7e4d359]

But the day corresponding to [MATH: (2,3)] actually has [MATH: y=3] hours of focused work. So, the line of best fit overestimates this day’s focused-work hours by
[MATH: 4.2 - 3 = 1.2 > 1.]
No other point is that far below the line, so this must be the day in question. Therefore, [MATH: 2] hours of meetings were recorded this day.
